sentences.text: Das Werk fragt auch nach der politischen Bedeutung des Körpers.
sentences.translation: The work also asks about the political significance of the body.

words.grammar: die Bedeutung · bedeuten (to mean) · bedeutend = significant, important
der Körper (nom.) · des Körpers (gen.) · genitive case: masculine nouns add -s

sentences.text: Berlin hat ein Problem.
sentences.translation: Berlin has a problem.
sentences.grammarNote: Subject–verb–object order. 'haben' (to have) in Präsens: ich habe, du hast, er/sie/es hat. 'ein Problem' is Akkusativ – the thing you 'have' is the object.

sentences.text: Die Stadt braucht mehr Bäume.
sentences.translation: The city needs more trees.
sentences.grammarNote: 'brauchen' (to need) follows the same pattern as 'haben': subject + verb + object. 'Bäume' is the plural of 'der Baum' (the tree) – German often adds an umlaut (a→ä, u→ü) to make plurals.

sentences.text: Die Berliner haben dafür gestimmt.
sentences.translation: Berliners voted for this.
sentences.grammarNote: Perfekt tense: 'haben' + past participle at the end. This is the most common past tense in spoken and written German. 'gestimmt' is the Partizip II of 'stimmen'. The verb comes last when the auxiliary 'haben' is used.

sentences.text: Das Ziel ist eine Million Bäume.
sentences.translation: The goal is one million trees.
sentences.grammarNote: 'sein' (to be) links two noun phrases: subject + ist + description. No Akkusativ here – after 'sein' German uses Nominativ on both sides (das Ziel = eine Million Bäume).

sentences.text: Aber der Senat ist zu langsam.
sentences.translation: But the Senate is too slow.
sentences.grammarNote: 'zu + adjective' means 'too + adjective', just like English. The adjective 'langsam' is used predicatively here (after 'sein'), so it has no ending – compare 'ein langsamer Senat' (attributive, with ending).

sentences.text: Die ersten Fristen sind schon vorbei.
sentences.translation: The first deadlines have already passed.
sentences.grammarNote: 'vorbei sein' is a fixed expression meaning 'to be over/past'. 'schon' (already) sits before the thing it emphasises. 'ersten' is an adjective with a strong ending in Nominativ plural after 'die'.

words.grammar: erst- · Nominativ · Plural · nach bestimmtem Artikel

sentences.text: Kritiker sagen: Das ist nicht gut.
sentences.translation: Critics say: That is not good.
sentences.grammarNote: Direct speech introduced by a colon – common in German news writing. 'nicht' negates the adjective: 'nicht gut' = not good. Notice 'Das' (that/this) as a neutral demonstrative pronoun pointing back to the situation.

articles.title: Wahl in Neukölln: Sarah Nagel bleibt

sentences.text: Sarah Nagel arbeitet in Neukölln.
sentences.translation: Sarah Nagel works in Neukölln.
sentences.grammarNote: Location after the verb: subject + verb + place. 'in + Dativ' for locations where something happens (staying in a place). Compare: 'Sie geht nach Neukölln' (direction, with nach) vs 'Sie arbeitet in Neukölln' (location, with in + Dativ).

sentences.text: Sie ist Politikerin.
sentences.translation: She is a politician.
sentences.grammarNote: Professions after 'sein' take no article in German: 'Sie ist Politikerin' – not 'eine Politikerin'. This is different from English ('She is a politician'). Same rule: 'Er ist Lehrer', 'Sie ist Ärztin'.

words.grammar: die Politikerin · Nominativ · Singular · kein Artikel nach sein

sentences.text: Viele Leute wollten sie abwählen.
sentences.translation: Many people wanted to vote her out.
sentences.grammarNote: Modal verb construction: modal (wollten) in second position + infinitive at the end. 'wollen' in Präteritum (simple past) – modals commonly use Präteritum even in spoken German. 'abwählen' is a separable verb (ab- + wählen), but in the infinitive the prefix stays attached.

sentences.text: 34 Verordnete haben gegen sie gestimmt.
sentences.translation: 34 assembly members voted against her.
sentences.grammarNote: Perfekt again: 'haben' + Partizip II at the end. 'gegen + Akkusativ' = against (someone). Note 'sie' here is Akkusativ (her), not the subject – the subject is '34 Verordnete'.

sentences.text: Aber das war nicht genug.
sentences.translation: But that was not enough.
sentences.grammarNote: 'war' is the Präteritum (simple past) of 'sein'. For 'sein' and 'haben', Germans use Präteritum rather than Perfekt even in casual speech – 'das war' sounds natural, while 'das ist gewesen' would be unusual.

sentences.text: Sie bleibt in ihrem Amt.
sentences.translation: She stays in her position.
sentences.grammarNote: 'in + Dativ' for location/state. 'ihrem' is the possessive adjective 'ihr' (her) in Dativ masculine/neuter – 'das Amt' is neuter, so Dativ = 'dem Amt' → 'ihrem Amt'. Possessives follow the same endings as 'ein/kein'.

sentences.text: Jetzt muss Neukölln die Arbeit machen.
sentences.translation: Now Neukölln must do the work.
sentences.grammarNote: When an adverb like 'jetzt' (now) starts the sentence, the subject and verb swap: 'jetzt + muss + Neukölln' (verb before subject). This is called inversion – the verb always stays in second position in German main clauses.

words.grammar: müssen · Präsens · 3. Person Singular · Modalverb · Position 2

sentences.text: Im Juni gibt es ein großes Fest in Neukölln.
sentences.translation: In June there is a big festival in Neukölln.
sentences.grammarNote: 'es gibt' (there is/there are) is an impersonal construction – 'es' is a placeholder, not a real subject. The thing that exists goes in Akkusativ: 'ein großes Fest'. 'Im Juni' = 'in dem Juni', contracted. Time expressions often come first.

words.grammar: es gibt · Präsens · unpersönlich · Akkusativ folgt
groß · Akkusativ · Singular · Neutrum · nach unbestimmtem Artikel

sentences.text: Es heißt 48 Stunden Neukölln.
sentences.translation: It is called 48 Hours Neukölln.
sentences.grammarNote: 'heißen' means both 'to be called' and 'to mean'. Here 'Es heißt …' = 'It is called …'. The name follows directly with no article or case change. A useful phrase to learn things: 'Wie heißt das?' = 'What is that called?'

words.grammar: die Stunde · Nominativ · Plural · in Eigenname

sentences.text: Das Festival ist für Kunst und Kultur.
sentences.translation: The festival is for art and culture.
sentences.grammarNote: 'für + Akkusativ' = for (something). Here 'Kunst und Kultur' are abstract nouns used without an article – very common in German for general concepts. Compare: 'für die Kunst' (for the art, specific) vs 'für Kunst' (for art in general).

words.grammar: die Kunst · Akkusativ · Singular · kein Artikel (allgemein)
die Kultur · Akkusativ · Singular · kein Artikel (allgemein)

sentences.text: Es findet schon zum 28. Mal statt.
sentences.translation: It is taking place for the 28th time.
sentences.grammarNote: 'stattfinden' is a separable verb: the prefix 'statt-' splits off and goes to the end – 'Es findet … statt'. In the infinitive it stays together: 'stattfinden'. 'zum 28. Mal' = 'for the 28th time'; 'zum' = 'zu dem' (Dativ).

words.grammar: stattfinden · Präsens · 3. Person Singular · trennbar · Stamm in Position 2

sentences.text: Viele Künstler aus dem Kiez machen mit.
sentences.translation: Many artists from the neighbourhood take part.
sentences.grammarNote: 'mitmachen' = to join in / take part. Another separable verb: 'mit' splits off to the end. 'aus dem Kiez' = from the neighbourhood – 'aus + Dativ' for origin or source. 'dem' is the Dativ article for masculine nouns (der Kiez → aus dem Kiez).

sentences.text: Der Eintritt ist kostenlos.
sentences.translation: Entry is free.
sentences.grammarNote: Predicative adjective: adjective after 'sein' has no ending – 'kostenlos', not 'kostenloser'. Compare attributive use: 'der kostenlose Eintritt' (the free entry, adjective before noun, needs an ending). This is a key German adjective rule.

words.grammar: kostenlos · Prädikativ · keine Endung nach sein

sentences.text: In Neukölln gibt es jetzt vier Azzam-Filialen.
sentences.translation: In Neukölln there are now four Azzam branches.
sentences.grammarNote: The sentence starts with a place ('In Neukölln'), so the verb 'gibt' comes before the subject placeholder 'es' – inversion. 'es gibt' + Akkusativ for 'there is/are'. Numbers before nouns need no article: 'vier Filialen', not 'die vier Filialen' (unless the specific ones are known).

words.grammar: es gibt · Präsens · unpersönlich · Inversion nach Ortsangabe

sentences.text: Azzam ist ein Supermarkt.
sentences.translation: Azzam is a supermarket.
sentences.grammarNote: Simple definition sentence: name + ist + indefinite article + noun. 'ein Supermarkt' uses the indefinite article 'ein' (masculine), agreeing with 'der Supermarkt'. This pattern is identical for introductions: 'Das ist ein Markt', 'Er ist ein Laden'.

sentences.text: Dort kauft man arabische und türkische Lebensmittel.
sentences.translation: There you can buy Arabic and Turkish food products.
sentences.grammarNote: 'man' is an impersonal pronoun meaning 'one / you / people in general' – it never refers to a specific person. The verb agrees as 3. Person Singular: 'man kauft'. 'Dort' (there) starts the sentence, triggering inversion: 'kauft man'. Adjective endings: 'arabische/türkische' are Akkusativ plural after no article.

words.grammar: arabisch · Akkusativ · Plural · kein Artikel → starke Endung -e

sentences.text: Viele Menschen aus dem Kiez kommen gern.
sentences.translation: Many people from the neighbourhood like to come.
sentences.grammarNote: 'gern + verb' expresses liking to do something – 'kommen gern' = like to come. 'gern' has no fixed position but usually comes near the end. It is the equivalent of 'mögen + infinitive' but simpler and more idiomatic.

words.grammar: aus · mit Dativ · dem = Dativ maskulin

sentences.text: Neukölln ist ein bunter Bezirk.
sentences.translation: Neukölln is a colourful / diverse borough.
sentences.grammarNote: Attributive adjective before a masculine noun: after 'ein' (indefinite article, masculine Nominativ), the adjective takes the ending '-er' – 'ein bunter Bezirk'. The article 'ein' doesn't show gender clearly (no -r), so the adjective does the work.

words.grammar: bunt · attributiv · Nominativ · Singular · maskulin · Endung -er nach ein

sentences.text: Hier leben Menschen aus vielen Ländern.
sentences.translation: People from many countries live here.
sentences.grammarNote: 'hier' (here) starts the sentence, so inversion occurs: 'leben Menschen' instead of 'Menschen leben'. 'aus vielen Ländern' = from many countries – 'aus + Dativ plural'. 'Ländern' is Dativ plural of 'das Land'; most German nouns add '-n' or '-en' in Dativ plural.

sentences.text: Bald ist Karneval der Kulturen in Berlin.
sentences.translation: Soon it is Carnival of Cultures in Berlin.
sentences.grammarNote: Adverb 'bald' (soon) at the start triggers inversion: 'ist' before the subject. 'Karneval der Kulturen' is a proper name – 'der Kulturen' is Genitiv plural (of cultures), which is how German forms possessive names: 'Karneval of the Cultures'.

words.grammar: die Kultur · Genitiv · Plural · in Eigenname

sentences.text: Das Fest ist jedes Jahr zu Pfingsten.
sentences.translation: The festival is every year at Pentecost.
sentences.grammarNote: 'jedes Jahr' is a time expression in Akkusativ used as an adverb (wie oft? = how often?). 'zu Pfingsten' = at Pentecost – 'zu' with festivals/holidays. 'Pfingsten' has no article, unlike most nouns.

words.grammar: zu · mit Dativ · bei Festen und Feiertagen

sentences.text: Es gibt Musik, Tanz und viele bunte Kostüme.
sentences.translation: There is music, dance and many colourful costumes.
sentences.grammarNote: 'es gibt' lists multiple things – all in Akkusativ. Abstract nouns 'Musik' and 'Tanz' have no article. 'viele bunte Kostüme' = many colourful costumes: 'viele' and 'bunte' are Akkusativ plural with no article, so both take strong endings (-e).

words.grammar: viel · Akkusativ · Plural · starke Endung -e · kein Artikel
bunt · Akkusativ · Plural · starke Endung -e · kein Artikel

sentences.text: Gruppen aus aller Welt nehmen teil.
sentences.translation: Groups from all over the world take part.
sentences.grammarNote: 'teilnehmen' is separable: 'nehmen' stays in second position, 'teil' goes to the end. 'aus aller Welt' is a fixed phrase meaning 'from all over the world' – 'aller' is Genitiv/Dativ of 'all', used without article in this expression.

words.grammar: teilnehmen · Präsens · 3. Person Plural · trennbar · Stamm in Position 2

sentences.text: Der Umzug geht durch Kreuzberg und Neukölln.
sentences.translation: The parade goes through Kreuzberg and Neukölln.
sentences.grammarNote: 'durch + Akkusativ' = through (movement across a space). Movement prepositions like 'durch', 'um', 'gegen', 'für' always take Akkusativ. Compare with location prepositions like 'in + Dativ' (staying somewhere). City names like Kreuzberg and Neukölln have no article.

words.grammar: durch · mit Akkusativ · Bewegung durch Raum

sentences.text: Es kommen jedes Jahr sehr viele Menschen.
sentences.translation: Very many people come every year.
sentences.grammarNote: Here 'Es' is a placeholder that allows 'jedes Jahr' (time) and 'sehr viele Menschen' (subject) to be arranged for emphasis. The real subject is 'sehr viele Menschen' – notice 'kommen' is plural to agree with it. 'sehr viele' = very many: 'sehr' intensifies 'viele'.

words.grammar: kommen · Präsens · 3. Person Plural · kongruiert mit Menschen

sentences.text: Der Sommer beginnt in Deutschland.
sentences.translation: Summer is beginning in Germany.
sentences.grammarNote: Subject–verb–location word order: subject (Der Sommer) + verb (beginnt) + place (in Deutschland). 'beginnen' (to begin) is regular in the Präsens: er/sie/es beginnt.

sentences.text: Die Temperaturen steigen auf 30 Grad.
sentences.translation: Temperatures are rising to 30 degrees.
sentences.grammarNote: 'steigen auf + Akkusativ' = to rise to (a value). Numbers combined with 'Grad' need no article: '30 Grad', not 'die 30 Grad'.

words.grammar: das Grad · same form singular and plural after numbers

sentences.text: Viele Menschen gehen ins Schwimmbad.
sentences.translation: Many people go to the swimming pool.
sentences.grammarNote: 'ins' = 'in das', contracted — Akkusativ, used for movement into a place. 'gehen' (to go) is regular here in the plural: sie gehen.

words.grammar: das Schwimmbad · compound: schwimmen (to swim) + Bad (bath)

sentences.text: Die Sonne scheint fast jeden Tag.
sentences.translation: The sun shines almost every day.
sentences.grammarNote: 'jeden Tag' (every day) is a time expression in Akkusativ with no preposition. 'scheinen' (to shine) is a strong verb: sie scheint (singular).

sentences.text: Das Wetter bleibt warm bis zum Wochenende.
sentences.translation: The weather stays warm until the weekend.
sentences.grammarNote: 'bleiben' (to stay) + adjective describes an ongoing state — 'bleibt warm' takes no ending on the predicate adjective. 'bis zum Wochenende' = until the weekend, a fixed combination with Dativ.

words.grammar: bis zu + dem → bis zum · Dativ

sentences.text: Viele Deutsche essen weniger Fleisch.
sentences.translation: Many Germans eat less meat.
sentences.grammarNote: 'weniger' (less) is the comparative of 'wenig' and stays unchanged before a noun. 'essen' (to eat) has no vowel change in the plural: wir/sie essen.

words.grammar: der/die Deutsche · Nominativ · Plural · adjective used as a noun

sentences.text: Eine neue Studie zeigt: Jeder fünfte Mensch isst vegetarisch.
sentences.translation: A new study shows: every fifth person eats vegetarian.
sentences.grammarNote: The colon introduces the study's finding, like in English. 'Jeder fünfte' = 'every fifth' — the ordinal number 'fünfte' takes a weak ending after 'jeder'. 'isst' is the irregular du/er-form of 'essen'.

words.grammar: fünf → fünfte · Ordinalzahl · schwache Endung nach jeder

sentences.text: Die Zahl wächst jedes Jahr.
sentences.translation: The number grows every year.
sentences.grammarNote: 'wachsen' (to grow) is a strong verb with a vowel change: er/sie/es wächst. 'jedes Jahr' is another Akkusativ time expression without a preposition.

words.grammar: wachsen · Präsens · 3. Person Singular · Vokalwechsel a→ä

sentences.text: Ärzte sagen: Gemüse ist gesund für das Herz.
sentences.translation: Doctors say: vegetables are healthy for the heart.
sentences.grammarNote: 'für + Akkusativ' = for (the benefit of). The predicative adjective 'gesund' after 'ist' takes no ending.

words.grammar: das Gemüse · uncountable, singular form used for the whole category
das Herz · Akkusativ · irregular neuter noun

sentences.text: Supermärkte verkaufen mehr pflanzliche Produkte.
sentences.translation: Supermarkets sell more plant-based products.
sentences.grammarNote: 'mehr' (more), like 'weniger', is invariable. 'pflanzliche' takes a strong plural ending in Akkusativ since there's no article before 'mehr'.

words.grammar: pflanzlich → pflanzliche · Akkusativ · Plural · starke Endung

articles.title: Neue App hilft bei der Zugfahrt

sentences.text: Die Deutsche Bahn hat eine neue App.
sentences.translation: Deutsche Bahn has a new app.
sentences.grammarNote: 'haben' + Akkusativ object: 'eine neue App'. 'Die Deutsche Bahn' (German Rail) still takes 'die' because 'Bahn' is a feminine noun.

sentences.text: Die App zeigt Verspätungen in Echtzeit.
sentences.translation: The app shows delays in real time.
sentences.grammarNote: 'in Echtzeit' (in real time) is a fixed adverbial phrase, Dativ after 'in' for a manner/state. 'Verspätungen' is the plural of 'die Verspätung'.

sentences.text: Reisende können den nächsten Zug einfach finden.
sentences.translation: Travelers can easily find the next train.
sentences.grammarNote: Modal verb 'können' (can) + infinitive at the end ('finden'). 'den nächsten Zug' is Akkusativ, the direct object of finden — 'nächsten' takes a weak ending after 'den'.

words.grammar: der/die Reisende · Nominativ · Plural · adjective used as a noun

sentences.text: Die App ist kostenlos für alle.
sentences.translation: The app is free for everyone.
sentences.grammarNote: Predicative adjective 'kostenlos' after 'ist' takes no ending. 'für alle' = for everyone, Akkusativ after 'für'.

words.grammar: kostenlos · Prädikativ · keine Endung nach sein

sentences.text: Viele Nutzer finden die App sehr praktisch.
sentences.translation: Many users find the app very practical.
sentences.grammarNote: Here 'finden' means 'to consider (something to be)', not 'to locate' — a common double meaning. 'sehr' intensifies 'praktisch'.

words.grammar: der Nutzer · Nominativ · Plural · same form singular/plural

articles.title: Rock am Ring: Tausende Fans feiern Musik

sentences.text: Rock am Ring ist ein großes Musikfestival.
sentences.translation: Rock am Ring is a big music festival.
sentences.grammarNote: Simple definition sentence: name + ist + indefinite article + adjective + noun. 'großes' takes the strong neuter ending after 'ein' (das Festival).

words.grammar: groß → großes · Nominativ · Singular · Neutrum · nach ein

sentences.text: Jedes Jahr kommen tausende Fans aus ganz Deutschland.
sentences.translation: Every year, thousands of fans come from all over Germany.
sentences.grammarNote: The time expression 'Jedes Jahr' starts the sentence, triggering inversion: verb (kommen) before subject (tausende Fans). 'aus ganz Deutschland' = from all over Germany.

words.grammar: tausend → tausende · Nominativ · Plural · lowercase when used loosely as 'thousands of'

sentences.text: Viele berühmte Bands spielen auf der Bühne.
sentences.translation: Many famous bands play on the stage.
sentences.grammarNote: 'auf + Dativ' for location (being on a surface). 'berühmte' is a strong plural adjective ending since there's no article before 'viele'.

words.grammar: berühmt → berühmte · Nominativ · Plural · starke Endung

sentences.text: Das Festival dauert drei Tage.
sentences.translation: The festival lasts three days.
sentences.grammarNote: 'dauern' (to last) takes a direct time-length object in Akkusativ with no preposition: 'dauert drei Tage'.

sentences.text: Die Fans campen zusammen auf einer großen Wiese.
sentences.translation: The fans camp together on a big meadow.
sentences.grammarNote: 'campen' is a borrowed English verb, conjugated regularly: sie campen. 'auf einer großen Wiese' is Dativ after 'auf' (location) — 'großen' takes the weak ending after 'einer'.

sentences.text: Der Herbst beginnt in Deutschland.
sentences.translation: Autumn is beginning in Germany.
sentences.grammarNote: Same pattern as 'Der Sommer beginnt' — subject + verb + location. 'der Herbst' (autumn) is masculine.

sentences.text: Die Blätter werden bunt und fallen von den Bäumen.
sentences.translation: The leaves turn colorful and fall from the trees.
sentences.grammarNote: 'werden' + adjective = to become/turn: 'werden bunt' = turn colorful. 'von + Dativ' shows origin: 'von den Bäumen' = from the trees.

sentences.text: Die Temperaturen fallen langsam.
sentences.translation: Temperatures are slowly falling.
sentences.grammarNote: 'fallen' (to fall) is a strong verb but regular in the plural Präsens: sie fallen. 'langsam' (slowly) has the same form as the adjective.

sentences.text: Viele Menschen tragen jetzt eine warme Jacke.
sentences.translation: Many people now wear a warm jacket.
sentences.grammarNote: 'tragen' is a strong verb: du/er/sie/es trägt, but wir/sie tragen (no change in plural). 'eine warme Jacke' is Akkusativ, weak ending after 'eine'.

sentences.text: Der Herbst ist für viele die schönste Jahreszeit.
sentences.translation: Autumn is, for many, the most beautiful season.
sentences.grammarNote: Superlative with 'der/die/das + -ste': 'die schönste' = the most beautiful. 'für viele' = for many (people), Akkusativ after 'für'.

words.grammar: schön → schönste · Superlativ · Nominativ · Singular · Femininum

articles.title: Das Oktoberfest in München lockt Millionen Besucher

sentences.text: Das Oktoberfest in München hat begonnen.
sentences.translation: The Oktoberfest in Munich has begun.
sentences.grammarNote: Perfekt tense: 'hat' + past participle 'begonnen' at the end. 'beginnen' is a strong verb with an irregular past participle.

words.grammar: beginnen · Perfekt · hat + begonnen · unregelmäßiges Partizip II

sentences.text: Millionen Besucher kommen jedes Jahr nach München.
sentences.translation: Millions of visitors come to Munich every year.
sentences.grammarNote: 'nach + Stadt' = to a city (direction). 'Millionen Besucher' needs no article or linking word before the noun, like other numbers.

words.grammar: der Besucher · Nominativ · Plural · same form singular/plural
nach · mit Dativ · Richtung zu Städten

sentences.text: Die Besucher trinken Bier und essen Brezeln.
sentences.translation: The visitors drink beer and eat pretzels.
sentences.grammarNote: Two verbs joined by 'und' — no change in word order since 'und' is a coordinating conjunction. 'Bier' and 'Brezeln' are direct objects (Akkusativ) with no article.

sentences.text: Viele Besucher tragen traditionelle Kleidung.
sentences.translation: Many visitors wear traditional clothing.
sentences.grammarNote: 'traditionelle Kleidung' is Akkusativ, strong plural ending since there's no article before 'traditionelle'; 'Kleidung' is uncountable and used generally here.

sentences.text: Das Fest dauert bis Anfang Oktober.
sentences.translation: The festival lasts until early October.
sentences.grammarNote: 'bis + time expression' = until. 'Anfang Oktober' (early October) is a fixed time phrase with no preposition needed before the month.

words.grammar: der Anfang · used adverbially before month names: Anfang Oktober

sentences.text: Jedes Jahr findet der Berlin-Marathon statt.
sentences.translation: Every year, the Berlin Marathon takes place.
sentences.grammarNote: Separable verb 'stattfinden': the prefix 'statt' goes to the end of the clause. 'Jedes Jahr' at the start triggers inversion.

sentences.text: Über vierzigtausend Läufer nehmen teil.
sentences.translation: Over forty thousand runners take part.
sentences.grammarNote: 'über' here means 'more than', not location. 'teilnehmen' is separable: 'teil' goes to the end of the clause.

words.grammar: der Läufer · Nominativ · Plural · same form singular/plural

sentences.text: Die Strecke führt durch die ganze Stadt.
sentences.translation: The route leads through the whole city.
sentences.grammarNote: 'durch + Akkusativ' = through (movement across). 'die ganze Stadt' = the whole city, 'ganze' takes a weak ending after 'die'.

sentences.text: Viele Zuschauer stehen am Straßenrand und jubeln.
sentences.translation: Many spectators stand at the roadside and cheer.
sentences.grammarNote: 'am Straßenrand' = 'an dem Straßenrand', contracted, Dativ for location. 'jubeln' (to cheer) is a regular weak verb.

words.grammar: der Zuschauer · Nominativ · Plural · same form singular/plural

sentences.text: Der Sieger läuft die Strecke in etwas mehr als zwei Stunden.
sentences.translation: The winner runs the route in just over two hours.
sentences.grammarNote: 'in + Dativ' for a time duration: 'in zwei Stunden' = in two hours. 'etwas mehr als' = a little more than, a fixed comparison phrase.

sentences.text: Immer mehr Deutsche kaufen ein Elektroauto.
sentences.translation: More and more Germans are buying an electric car.
sentences.grammarNote: 'immer mehr' = more and more, a fixed intensifying phrase. 'ein Elektroauto' is Akkusativ, direct object of 'kaufen'.

sentences.text: Die Verkäufe sind in diesem Jahr stark gestiegen.
sentences.translation: Sales have risen sharply this year.
sentences.grammarNote: Perfekt with 'sein' (not 'haben') because 'steigen' describes a change of state. 'stark' modifies 'gestiegen' like an adverb.

sentences.text: Ein Elektroauto braucht keine Tankstelle.
sentences.translation: An electric car doesn't need a gas station.
sentences.grammarNote: 'keine' negates the indefinite article before a feminine noun: 'keine Tankstelle' = no gas station.

sentences.text: Die Regierung unterstützt den Kauf mit Geld.
sentences.translation: The government supports the purchase with money.
sentences.grammarNote: 'mit + Dativ' = with (a means). 'den Kauf' is Akkusativ, the direct object of 'unterstützt'.

sentences.text: Experten erwarten noch mehr Elektroautos auf den Straßen.
sentences.translation: Experts expect even more electric cars on the roads.
sentences.grammarNote: 'noch mehr' = even more, intensifying 'mehr'. 'auf + Dativ' for location: 'auf den Straßen' = on the roads.
